basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma '« Et dixit Dominus Deus ad mulierem: Quare hoc fecisti? Quae respondit: Serpens decepit'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: « Et dixit Dominus Deus ad mulierem: Quare hoc fecisti? Quae respondit: Serpens decepit me, et comedi. Nec ista confitetur peccatum, sed in alterum refert, impari sexu, pari fastu, Serpens, inquit, decepit me et comedi; quasi cujusquam suasio praecepto Dei debuerit anteponi. » Et ipsa autem culpae causam in Creatorem refert, qui serpentem in paradiso per quem deciperetur, creaverit.
